== Biography ==
Allen was born about 1839.<ref>Based on age 18 at marriage.</ref>
He is the son of [[Glasgow-1701|James Glasgow]],  and lived at Killycurragh as of 1857.

On 2 Jan 1857 at Oritor Presbyterian, he married Esther Henry of Drumnamalta, daughter of Wm Henry, farmer. Witnessed by Thomas John Allen and John Henry.
<ref>[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/66d1873269665 Allen Glasgow, Esther Henry, 1857, Cookstown] at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages</ref>

He passed away 31 Dec 1925.
<ref>GRONI search: D/1926/99/1009/26/165	Allen	Glasgow	31st December 1925	87		Male	Cookstown</ref>
He is buried at Clare Churchyard in a family plot.
<ref>[[Space:Kildress_Church_of_Ireland_Churchyard%2C_Cookstown%2C_Tyrone]] - Allan Glasgow</ref>
== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1701]] is assessed at 98% (proved). Allen's 1857 marriage account names father James and Killycurragh residence. His explicit brotherhood with Thomas James and Nancy's sibling list identify the selected James junior, rather than another local James.

Selected Glasgow-1701 fatherhood of Glasgow-1703; maternal identity and upstream ancestry are separate.

Next useful test: Compare original 1857 marriage with Nancy's 1896 notice.

Source basis already held: [https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/66d1873269665 Allen Glasgow, Esther Henry, 1857, Cookstown (https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/66d1873269665) at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


He was definitely the brother of [[Glasgow-1700|Thomas James Glasgow (abt.1833-1915)]], appearing as Brother in his obituary.

Allen, S.J. and Thomas J. Glasgow appear at the funeral of [[Allen-53097|Thomas John Allen (1830-1907)]] as cousins.

There is an 1891 marriage of [[Glasgow-2262 |William James Glasgow]](34) , merchant, son of Allan Glasgow, farmer.  He is at Cookstown town though, would need more checking to match this. The wife is [[Moore-73322 |Rebecca Jane Moore]] and witnesses Joseph Glasgow and Johanna McClelland.
[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/649fb52565946 Link]

* Belfast News-Letter 1879: his eldest daughter Mary "Minnie" marries WIlliam Henry of Killycurragh.
